plan.summary: This 4-week opening block is a simple off-camp build for boxing with one weekly bodyweight-only session. Week 1 establishes a baseline on the main lower-body and upper-body strength patterns using hard bodyweight rep tests so future progress is easy to track, and the main training starts in Week 2. With only one S&C session per week, the plan keeps power first, then strength work, then trunk and neck in brief safe doses.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build basic full-body strength, landing control, trunk stiffness, and simple explosive intent with low-equipment work.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the hardest bodyweight variations and keep power output sharp without adding unnecessary fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength with a smaller dose and shift more emphasis toward crisp speed and reactive boxing-relevant output.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Reset between reps and jump as high and fast as you can. Land softly and stop if height drops off.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a simpler no-dip pause before takeoff.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump to Stable Surface
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if a safe box or step is available and landing is quiet and controlled.

exercises.name: Push-Up Test Set
exercises.notes: Warm up with a few easy sets, then perform 1 all-out clean set and stop when form breaks. This sets your baseline for future upper-body strength work.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then perform one hard max-rep set with strict form. Log the reps so the app can track your baseline.

performanceTarget.prompt: Beat your Week 1 strict rep total over the next block without sacrificing range or body position.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up Test Set
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if floor push-ups are not yet clean. Keep the same body angle each time you retest.

exercises.name: Split Squat Test Set
exercises.notes: Warm up with easy practice reps, then perform 1 hard set per side with bodyweight and clean depth. This sets your baseline for single-leg lower-body strength endurance.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then perform one hard set per side with clean control. Log reps on both legs so the app can track your baseline.

performanceTarget.prompt: Aim to improve the weaker side first and keep both sides even.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge Test Set
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if split squats bother the knees or balance is limited.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Row Under Table or Bar
exercises.notes: Use a stable setup only. Pull chest toward the edge, keep the body straight, and stop 1-2 reps before form breaks.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Towel Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if the anchor is very secure and you can keep tension smooth.

substitutionOptions.name: Prone Snow Angel
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if no safe row setup is available. Move slowly and squeeze the upper back hard.

exercises.name: Front Plank
exercises.notes: Brace hard, ribs down, glutes tight, and breathe behind the brace.

substitutionOptions.name: Hollow Body Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a harder anterior trunk option.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the plank position irritates the low back.

exercises.name: Supine Neck Lift
exercises.notes: Small controlled range only. Move slowly and stop immediately if you feel pain, dizziness, or a headache.

substitutionOptions.name: Towel Isometric Neck Flexion
substitutionOptions.notes: Use light hand pressure and hold each rep for 5-8 seconds.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Every rep should look sharp and springy. Rest enough to keep jump quality high.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a simpler jump with a dead-stop start.

exercises.name: 1a. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Leave 1-2 good reps in reserve. Full range, body straight, and drive up fast.

performanceTarget.prompt: Stay in the target rep range with clean reps before progressing to a harder variation.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard push-ups are still short of the rep target.

substitutionOptions.name: Close-Grip Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard push-ups are too easy and you want more triceps emphasis.

exercises.name: 1b. Bodyweight Row Under Table or Bar
exercises.notes: Pull with the upper back, pause briefly at the top, and keep the body rigid.

performanceTarget.prompt: Add reps first, then move to a more challenging body angle.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Towel Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only with a secure setup and smooth controlled reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Prone Snow Angel
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if no safe pulling setup is available.

exercises.name: 2a. Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use a steady tempo, reach full depth you can control, and drive through the front foot.

performanceTarget.prompt: Build even reps on both legs before using a harder variation.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the split squat stance feels awkward or bothers the knees.

substitutionOptions.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if standard split squats are already easy and stable.

exercises.name: 2b. Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Lock the ribs down and finish with the glute, not the low back.

substitutionOptions.name: Two-Leg Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if single-leg control is not there yet.

substitutionOptions.name: Hamstring Walkout
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a harder posterior-chain bodyweight option.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: Straight line from head to heel. Keep the hips tall and do not rotate.

substitutionOptions.name: Copenhagen Side Plank Short Lever
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a harder groin and trunk challenge.

exercises.name: Prone Neck Lift
exercises.notes: Lift gently, keep the chin tucked slightly, and move with control only.

substitutionOptions.name: Towel Isometric Neck Extension
substitutionOptions.notes: Use light hand pressure and smooth holds.

exercises.name: Skater Jump to Stick
exercises.notes: Jump laterally with control, stick the landing for a full count, and keep the knee stacked over the foot.

substitutionOptions.name: Lateral Line Hop to Stick
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if space is limited or the skater jump is too advanced.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if lateral landings are not yet clean.

exercises.notes: Smooth down, powerful up, and stop before your hips sag or head reaches first.

performanceTarget.prompt: Try to improve your best strict set from last week while keeping 1 rep in reserve.

substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard push-ups are comfortably above the rep range.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Towel Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only with a very secure setup.

substitutionOptions.name: Prone Snow Angel
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if no pulling setup is available.
